sections.markdown: The **Wretch** is one of the starting origins in Elden Ring. Unlike the other origins, this one only starts out with one piece of equipment, the Club.

Armaments**

Tools**

sections.heading: Build Optimization
sections.markdown: For people who wish to select an origin that will have the most optimal stat distribution for a build with the fewest stat points wasted, Wretch does not specialize by lowering any particular stat below 10 and as a result is rarely the optimal choice - but not never.

sections.heading: Omnicaster
sections.markdown: A build that uses Intelligence, Faith and Arcane to cast every type of spell available is one where the Wretch is surprisingly the most efficient, sharing this accolade with the Astrologer. Every other origin wastes more points in this type of build than the Wretch does, which arguably gives the Wretch more build utility than the Warrior or Confessor overall.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
__NOTOC__
Weapons**, also known as **Armaments**, are equipment items in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree.

Weapons scale in power based on the player's attributes. Several weapons can be wielded two-handed, affecting their attack strength and animation patterns. For keyboard controls, the command to switch to two-handed mode is to hold **E** and then click the attack button of the weapon in question.

There are two types of Armaments: generic weapons that are upgraded with Smithing Stones and unique weapons, which are bolstered with Somber Smithing Stones. Armaments may be improved by interacting with Smithing Master Hewg, Smithing Master Iji, or the Smithing Table at the Church of Elleh. Armaments of both types fall into one of four categories: Melee Armaments, Ranged Armaments, Catalysts, and Shields.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: White Mask Varré** (白面のヴァレー) is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Varré is an enigmatic man who dresses as a war surgeon. War Surgeons, despite their name, are not surgeons or doctors. They act as mercy killers on battlefields, putting dying soldiers out of their misery as quickly as possible by delivering final blows. Varré was a war surgeon prior to his association with Mohg.

Varré was abducted by Mohg against his will along with various other war surgeons, however it was noted that Varré was particularly talented with blood incantations, and that of all the war surgeons abducted he was the only one able to "tame" Mohg's cursed blood. Somewhere along the way Varré came to genuinely worship Mohg. If game data is accessed to remove his mask, you can see Mohg's emblem painted on his forehead.

Varré is generally regarded as enticing but deceitful. He is eloquent and is kind to the Tarnished at first, but this appears to be a front as his personality can change dramatically if elicited by disobedience. For example: He will try to suggest he is helping the Tarnished, and refers to them with the pet name "Lambkin", but if provoked he consequently will refer to them as a "runt" and "low born". If the tarnished refuses Varré's offer to join Mohg, then he will indignantly remark that they must have misheard his request, and that he will wait "for your ears to clean out."

Varré seems to also harbor some level of sadism, or in the least, an indifference to the pain of others. He asks the Tarnished to soak a cloth in a finger maiden's blood and remarks that since they have no maiden of their own, "any maiden will do". When he injects the tarnished with royal blood and they scream in pain, he chuckles in a shocked tone and says "clench your teeth, or something". When the ritual is completed he will remark that the tarnished as "the sweetest scream". If attacked at the Rose church he will remark upon killing the tarnished that "materials of quality are so hard to find these days", revealing that he only ever thought of the Tarnished as a material or tool.

sections.heading: Events in Game
sections.markdown:
The Tarnished first encounters him in Limgrave, after exiting the Stranded Graveyard, where he offers them guidance, noticing that they are not accompanied by a Finger Maiden. He advises the Tarnished to journey to Stormveil Castle and challenge Godrick the Grafted for his Great Rune, and recommends that they visit the Roundtable Hold.

The Tarnished encounters him again in Liurnia of the Lakes, outside the Rose Church. Here, he tests the Tarnished's dedication to the Two Fingers, expressing his own doubts about the veracity of their words. If the Tarnished shares his concerns, he reveals himself to be a loyal disciple of Mohg, Lord of Blood, and offers the Tarnished the opportunity to join his new dynasty. After the Tarnished completes their initiation, by soaking a cloth in the blood of a maiden, Varré awards them with a medal which will grant them audience with Mohg when the time is right. He also injects the Tarnished's finger with noble blood, allowing them to invade other worlds.

The Tarnished journeys to Mohgwyn Palace where they encounter Varré for the final time, invading his world and defeating him. Varré dies on the ground of Mohgwyn Palace after blessing Mohg's dynasty.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown:
- Limgrave (The First Step)

Just past the Site of Grace. Will leave a message in his spot after talking with Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold.

- Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)

At the entrance of the Rose Church, to the west of the Site of Grace.

- Mohgwyn Palace (Dynasty Mausoleum Entrance)

His invasion sign is located in the hallway before the Dynasty Mausoleum Midpoint Site of Grace. After defeating him, Varré will be found laying on the floor close to where the sign previously was.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Limgrave (The First Step)
 - *(Optional)* Talk to Varré next to The First Step Site of Grace.
 - *(Optional)* After visiting the Roundtable Hold, return to Varré and exhaust his dialogue.
 - *(Optional)* After obtaining a Great Rune, return to Varré and exhaust his dialogue.
 - *(Optional)* After talking to Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold, read the message he leaves behind to receive the "Bravo!" Gesture.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)
 - As he moves at the entrance of the Rose Church after speaking with Enia, talk to him, selecting **They didn't seem right**, and exhaust his dialogues to receive Festering Bloody Finger x5.
1. Altus Plateau (Road of Iniquity Side Path)
 - Interact with the invasion sign of Magnus the Beast Claw, found at the Writheblood Ruins south-west of the Site of Grace, and either defeat him or simply invade him three times. Invading actual players with the Festering Bloody Fingers three times is also enough to progress Varré's questline.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)
 - Return to Varré to receive the Lord of Blood's Favor, which needs to be coated in a maiden's blood. The followings options are available:
 - The corpse of your Finger Maiden in the Chapel of Anticipation, which requires using an Imbued Sword Key at the Four Bellfries of Liurnia.
 - Vyke's Finger Maiden in the Church of Inhibition of Liurnia.
 - Killing Irina of Morne or, if already deceased, Lightseeker Hyetta at any of their locations.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake)
 - Return to Varré to receive the Bloody Finger, then talk to him again to receive the Pureblood Knight's Medal.
1. Mohgwyn Palace (Dynasty Mausoleum Entrance)
 - Reaching Mohgwyn Palace either through the Pureblood Knight's Medal or the Waygate in Consacrated Snowfield, interact with Varré's invasion sign in the hallway right before Dynasty Mausoleum Midpoint Site of Grace. Once defeated, he'll drop Festering Bloody Finger x6, Rune Arc x1 and Furlcalling Finger Remedy x1.
 - Talk to him near where his invasion sign was and, exhausting his dialogues, he'll die dropping Varré's Bouquet.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Wolves** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: They are roving beasts that may attack in packs. The common wolf is widespread throughout the wilds of the Lands Between, almost always encountered in packs and forewarned by its characteristic howl. Their packs are usually led by a tougher specimen distinguished by their color. They are hostile but relatively easy to avoid. They cannot be outrun on foot.

sections.heading: Wolf
sections.markdown: Grey wolves, the most common variety found in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: White Wolf
sections.markdown: Larger wolves with white fur. They are often found among packs of standard grey wolves.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Occasionally, wolves can be encountered attacking other entities. Notably, in a gorge near the Third Church of Marika, a large pack of them can be found swarming a Runebear. The wolves will lose handily if the Tarnished does not intervene.
- Three wolves of the regular variety can be summoned using the Lone Wolf Ashes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Wolves that drop from the sky in a gust at specific areas are a literal howling wind.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Wing of Astel** is a Curved Sword, a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Found inside a chest in Uhl Palace Ruins above a Withered Astel, located in Ainsel River and only reachable from Ainsel River Main.

More specifically, from Ainsel River Main site of grace and head down the tunnel. Take the left split in the road, guarded by a Hardhead Giant Ant, and follow the cliffside path to a stone structure with the chest.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Has a 20% damage bonus against Gravity-affinity enemies.
- Standing regular and charged heavy attacks, and dodging while charging a heavy attack also throws out one and two and one Magic beams respectively, in addition to the normal parts of a heavy attack. Since both parts can hit the same enemy, this weapon deals greatly increase damage and Stance damage on hit, at no FP cost.
- This weapon's variant of Unique Skill: Nebula is different from Bastard's Stars.
- The skill's damage is increased by Spellblade's Set (though not the heavy attack beams).
- Cannot be buffed or infused with Ashes of War.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.markdown: The **Winged Scythe** is a Reaper and Melee Armament in Elden Ring

sections.heading: Unique Skill
sections.markdown:
- Angel's Wings
 - Jump and imbue the wing-blade of the armament with light, then deliver a slashing attack on the enemy.
 - The white wings impede recovery actions using a Flask of Crimson Tears.
 - The skill only disables using the Flask of Crimson Tears of other players and player-style NPC invaders. Non-player-style enemies, such as Haligtree Knights and Depraved Perfumers, can still heal using their flasks.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Location**: Tombsward Ruins
- The Winged Scythe is found in a treasure chest in the underground cellar at the Tombsward Ruins, located on the western Weeping Peninsula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Winged Scythe can be strengthened to **+10** with Somber Smithing Stones.
- It scales best with Dexterity and Faith, with the latter having stronger scaling. However, it gains 3% more AR on a split Dexterity/Faith build, if somewhat more split between damage types.
- The Battle Art generates sacred White light and soft white feathers.
- An uneven pair of white-feathered wings affixed to an octagonal pole, the Winged Scythe features carved reliefs of bearded elders, possibly depicting the Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statues. Robed, bald-headed men, seen elsewhere on Ancient Dynasty stelae and obelisks, stand side-by-side to form a band just below the wing-like blades. Positioned above them is a different bearded figure, his features obscured beneath his dark, shadowy hood, similar to the certain skeleton statues found in catacombs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The skill produces unique white feather visual effects.
- This weapon is superficially similar to the shape of the Ancestral Followers' Greathorn Hammers, horns carved with tree ring-like markings.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Weeping Peninsula** is a subregion located to the south of Limgrave in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Weeping Peninsula is a crescent-shaped landmass at the southernmost tip of the Lands Between. It is named for its unceasing rainfall, which gives the impression of a land in perpetual lament. The landscape is marked by steep cliffs, deep ravines, poison swamps, and a mournful atmosphere.

To the northeast, the Bridge of Sacrifice connects the peninsula to Limgrave proper. A Rosus Statue overlooks the bridge from the east, guiding the dead to the Impaler's Catacombs on the northeastern shore. Nearby, the Forest Lookout Tower monitors the Demi-Human Forest Ruins, and south of Rosus lies both an area struck by starfall and the sorcerous Oridys's Rise.

At the center of the peninsula is a plateau dominated by a minor Erdtree and Radagon's Church of Pilgrimage. The area is home to a Erdtree Guardians and Miranda Blossoms. Rows of ancient black stone ruins flank the plateau, while fallen ruins are embedded in the earth throughout the region.

West of the plateau is Tombsward, where a Wandering Mausoleum tolling solemnly on the plain. This area, and the Fourth Church of Marika, are guarded by a group of Mausoleum Soldiers. A large number of Putrid Corpses aimlessly wander the littered western beach. The Tower of Return rises from the southwest, offering safe passage to the base of Erdtree.

The south is home to Castle Morne, located at the peninsula’s southernmost tip. The road to the castle passes through a demolished stone rampart before reaching its gates. Castle Morne was once the site of a storied battle between a lone revenger and Godfrey, First Elden Lord. Today, it is under the stewardship of Castellan Edgar, appointed by Godrick the Grafted. However, the castle has fallen into disarray following a revolt by its Misbegotten workers.

sections.heading: Passive Ability
sections.markdown:
Confluence — *"Ally's execution of art enables additional art activation regardless of gauge."*

The Ultimate Art Gauge fills and glows purple for **5 seconds** after an ally activates their Ultimate Art. The Undertaker can activate her Ultimate Art during this window, even if her Gauge was previously empty.

sections.heading: Character Skill
sections.markdown:
Trance — *"Bloodletting triggers the power of the loathsome hex"* (Cooldown duration: **14 seconds**)

Trance has no startup animation and can be activated at any time, even during an animation. Upon activation, Trance instantly applies a self-buff that lasts for eight (8) seconds with the following effects:
- Fully replenishes Stamina
- +35% to all Damage Negation stats
- +10% Attack Power
- Successive Attacks increase Attack Power by +10% for the remaining duration of the ability (required number of hits varies with Weapon Class).
- Increased Poise
- Sprint faster and at no Stamina cost
- Quick Dodge — Undertaker can act faster after dodging, but her invincibility during each dodge is reduced. At 30 FPS, her dodge animations have two fewer invincibility and recovery frames when the ability is activated.

Empowered Trance: If the Ultimate Art Gauge is full, Undertaker can fully consume it to empower Trance by holding down the Character Skill input or by pressing both L2 and R2 while holding Triangle (L1+R1+Y on Xbox). Empowered Trance adds the following effects:
- Extends duration from 8 to 15 seconds
- Attack Power significantly increased
- Automatically Dodge

The skill icon drains to indicate the remaining time for Trance. The 14-second cooldown begins when it ends. Reactivating Trance ends the effect early, reducing the effective cooldown duration.

Loathsome Hex — *"Pull out uncanny bone from body, speed toward target, and strike."*

The Undertaker pulls a long spine from her mouth and surges toward her target, dealing damage to anything in her way. This ability allows her to reach her target from great distances quickly and can be activated even mid-air.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Traitorous Straghess**, also known as the **Dreglord**, is one of the Nightlord bosses included in the expansion for Elden Ring Nightreign. When its health is depleted, it gains a second health bar by transforming into **Pure Impulse Straghess**.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Traitorous Dreglord Straghess is a large, staff-wielding humanoid boss formed from discarded corpses. The fight opens with slow, clearly telegraphed attacks, allowing consistent windows for evasion and counterattacks. At roughly 50% health, Straghess enters its second phase. It begins using attacks and spells that inflict Scarlet Rot and control space or block movement, sharply increasing the difficulty. Straghess also summons Putrid Corpses and Rotmounds that impede and trap the players.

Upon depletion of its health bar, **Traitorous Straghess** gains a second health bar and transforms into **Pure Impulse Straghess**, initiating the third and most demanding phase. Still applying Scarlet Rot, it becomes a markedly agile and erratic melee attacker, punishing players who overextend or fail to adjust to the faster tempo. Pure Impulse Straghess frequently disengages before re-entering with high-speed lunges and unrelenting attack combos, making sustained pressure difficult to maintain. It enters the fourth phase at approximately half health, at which point it summons pillars of flesh throughout the arena. These obstructions conceal its approach and allow it to trigger a wide explosive attack, forcing players to track its position while remaining constantly mobile.

They are quite tanky, draw aggro very well, and will be summoned at the summoning monument instead of at your side, meaning they will be in the perfect spot to distract #2.

sections.markdown: Winged Sword Insignia** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Obtained from Stillwater Cave in southern Liurnia of the Lakes, by defeating the Cleanrot Knight boss.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 3%/5%/10%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point.

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hit towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive).
 - These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land.
 - For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive.
- For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count.
- Can be worn together with the Millicent's Prosthesis to stack the effect, but not with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia.
- Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy.
 - An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice.
 - This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

That is, in some scenarios, performing an additional attack within a sequence would cause attack power to decrease, rather than increase. This could be observed when using the Dagger and Short Sword weapons. This effect could be observed for the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia as well.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Scaling is a mechanic in Elden Ring. Most weapons possess scaling values, which cause the weapon's effectiveness to increase in accordance with an associated stat. Weapons can scale with Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith or Arcane. Scaling affinity with each stat is signified by a letter icon on the weapon's information.

Attribute scaling impacts:

- Attack Power
- Sorcery Scaling and Incantation Scaling, with the *base damage* calculated as 100 since the actual damage varies by spell
- Poison, Blood Loss, Sleep, and Madness, if the weapon has Arcane attribute scaling

Scaling doesn't affect poise damage or stamina damage.

sections.heading: Scaling Values
sections.markdown:
The letter grades that are used to represent a weapon's scaling affinity is only a rough guide of a weapon's potential. These grades are derived from a scaling value, which is an invisible number that determines the exact amount of damage you receive from scaling. The scaling values that each letter can represent are:

- E: 1.75

The formula for calculating a weapon's scaling damage is:

 
Scaling value*Base damage\left ( \frac{stat scaling}{100} \right ) 
Base damage* is the damage of the weapon before any scaling is applied, and *stat scaling* is a value that is gained by increasing the relevant attribute. Increasing both of these values will also increase the bonus damage received from scaling, which means that a weapon with lower base damage but a higher scaling value will not necessarily gain more scaling.

sections.heading: Attribute Requirements
sections.markdown:
Most weapons have a minimum requirement for each attribute they scale with. If that requirement is not met, anything that scales with that attribute receives no scaling, and instead takes a -40% penalty.

For example, the Club has 103 base Physical Attack Power, and Strength scaling with a requirement of 10. A character with only 9 Strength would have 61 Physical Attack Power (103 - 42).

sections.heading: Stat Scaling
sections.markdown:
This value increases as the associated stat increases, varying somewhat depending on if the used affinity is physical (Standard, Heavy, Keen, Quality, or Occult) or non-physical (Fire, Flame Art, Lightning, Sacred, Magic, Cold, Blood, or Poison).
Physical affinity values
- Stat at 10: 15
- Stat at 20: 35
- Stat at 30: 46.5
- Stat at 40: 57.5
- Stat at 50: 67.5
- Stat at 60: 75
- Stat at 70: 82.5
- Stat at 80: 90
- Stat at 90: 92.5
- Stat at 99: 96

As can be seen, for physical affinities the biggest increase is from increasing a stat from 10 to 20, before falling of bit-by-bit from 20 to 40, then 40 to 50, and then 50 to 80, until it finally slows down to a crawl from 80 to 99.
Non-physical affinity values
- Stat at 10: 19
- Stat at 20: 40
- Stat at 30: 53
- Stat at 40: 66.5
- Stat at 50: 80
- Stat at 60: 85
- Stat at 70: 90
- Stat at 80: 95
- Stat at 90: 97.5
- Stat at 99: 100

For non-physical affinities, however, the increase is more steady. It still falls of heavily after the 10 to 20 stretch but after that remains steady with the scaling (most notably reaching the same amount of scaling by 50 as physical affinities don't get until almost reaching 70) until reaching 50, where after the scaling slows down to less than half until the stat reaches 80 and halves against for the final stretch to reach 99.
Spell tools
Spell tools (Staves and Sacred Seals) uses one of three different scaling rates depending on whether or not they scale with only one stat, scales with more than one stat, or if it's the Demi-Human Queen's Staff. The exception to this is the Prince of Death's Staff (PDS) which despite being a Staff that scales with more than one stat uses the more backloaded "one stat" scaling, making it require a large amount of both Intelligence and Faith to attain good results.

More specifically, those that scales with one stat (and the PDS) start strong and gain stronger scaling after reaching 25 in the stat and then again after reaching 60, until finally dropping off hard upon eventually reaching 80 in that stat.

Scaling with more than one stat initially scales rather poorly before skyrocketing to being much, much stronger in scaling for a stat upon getting to 15 in that stat until 30, were after it falls to more normal, "one stat" levels of scaling and then increases become insignificant after reaching 45 in that stat.

The Demi-Human Queen's Staff is effectively the inverse of regular "one stat" scaling with exceptional scaling prior to reaching 20 in Intelligence and then being weaker until it reaches 40 and after that it becomes even weaker.
Status Effects scaling

sections.heading: Increasing Scaling Values
sections.markdown:
All weapons increase their scaling values by being upgraded. All weapons upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones gain an extra 8% of their base scaling per upgrade level, while other weapons gain 2% by default.

Weapons that can be infused with ashes of war can gain affinities which alter both the base damage and the scaling values, affecting how different stats increase scaling damage. There is no universal formula for how infusion changes the values of a weapon and different weapons are changed by an infusion in different, seemingly arbitrary ways.

sections.markdown: Withered Astels**, also known as **Malformed Stars**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Malformed Stars are insect-like creatures with long bodies comprised of spheres. They have spindly, multi-jointed limbs that end with six-digited hands, translucent wings, and humanoid skulls. Visually, they are almost identical to Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, but the spheres composing their torsos are grey.

Born in a lightless abyss in the far beyond, they arrived to the Lands Between on falling stars. Withered Astels are typically found hanging from the ceilings of caves, and will fire rocks at the player from a distance with Gravity Sorceries.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Astel in Perfumer's Grotto is also visible from Altus Tunnel and will attack there.

- Very low Stance, easily broken with one or two heavy jumping attacks.

- For the one in Perfumer's Grotto and Altus Tunnel, the former location has direct access to it for either melee or ranged attacks while the latter can only reach it with very long ranged weapons such as Bows. The fight isn't very complicated, with almost no cover and in the Altus Tunnel one can still run up and down the branches while surviving its assault.

- For Uhl Palace Ruins stick close to the walls if taking the lower paths, so its attacks can hit. To reach the platform the Malformed Star is on, head up some fallen pillars to the right and then the cliffside.

- Ainsel River Main is similar to the Uhl Palace Ruins location, except the Malformed Star is already reachable from ground level and does not require any platforming.

- The Fallingstar Beasts are likely another variant of Astel. They have the same face and tails, but the ferromagnetic beasts are covered in stone and iron filings.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Found at a sap collection basin on top of some cliffs west of Capital Outskirts' Minor Erdtree and east of Hermit Merchant's Shack.
It is guarded by a group of Skeletal Slugs along with an additional Deathbird at night.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: When mixed into the Flask of Wondrous Physick and used, greatly increases the user's equip load by 450% for 3 minutes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- A 450% increase in equip load is effectively the same as multiplying maximum equip load with 5.5.
- Potentially very useful in that it let's the Tarnished combine their heaviest armor with their heaviest armaments while still keeping at a medium load, but also carries the danger of getting stuck in Heavy Load - or worse, Overloaded - should it run out at an inopportune moment.
 - Even with the Prophet Origin's low Endurance of 8 this will boost its maximum equip load from 45 to 247.5, and therefore increase the thresholds for its light and medium loads from 13.5 and 31.5 to 74.25 and 173.25. This makes it possible to carry the heavy Bull-Goat Set and its 63 weight while still keeping a light load and its much longer rolls, if not with a lot of weight to spare.
 - Be wary that unless equip load is kept under 15.6% of the maximum while under the effect of this tear, its effect expiring will send the user straight into heavy load. Additionally, being above 22.2% of maximum equipment load while under the tear's effect leads to being overloaded when it ends.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Armed with a greatsword and a buckler, the Wylder also relies on a wrist-mounted stake driver, capable of launching a grappling hook and priming an explosive stake. The Wylder wears a blue tunic adorned with arcane sigils over sleek, medium armor. The wing motifs flanking his helmet mark him as a swift and resourceful champion.
- His preferred weapon type is Greatswords, with which he has a unique moveset.

- Ultimate Art: Onslaught Stake – *"Powerful single attack that launches an iron stake with a great explosion."*

- The winged helmet is evocative of , the Roman god , and Malenia, Blade of Miquella.

 - Around his thighs is a viking boat.

sections.markdown: Zamor Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Zamor Knights are tall, slender humanoids with long, silver hair, and ornate masks, who move with elegance and cloak themselves in icy gales. This clan of warriors resides in the Zamor Ruins on the Mountaintops of the Giants and wield rimed curved swords imbued with frost.

They deal Slash damage and apply Frostbite buildup. They are vulnerable to Fire and Lightning damage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: The knights of Zamor have long practiced cold sorceries on the snowy northern mountaintops in devotion to winter. Since time immemorial, they have waged an enduring and bitter feud with the Fire Giants over the Flame Peak. They fought heroically alongside Queen Marika and Lord Godfrey in the War Against the Giants, some of them continuing to serve him, becoming guardians of the Hero's Graves of the Mountaintops and Altus, after the War of the Ancient Dragons. A single Ancient Heroes of Zamor was punished by Radagon and imprisoned close to the beach from where the Tarnished would leave the Lands Between. While the majority of Zamor Knights remained to protect their ancestral home, their Town of Zamor would be ultimately destroyed at some point.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - Zamor Knights can be parried and riposted.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Wings of the Storm** were a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Wings of the Storm were Engvall and Oleg, a pair of departed Banished Knights who were known as heroes in the Lands Between. They gained notoriety during the Shattering, their efforts earning them clemency from Morgott, the Omen King, who invited them to join his ranks.

The Grace-Given Lord's offer ultimately split the heroic Stormveil duo. Oleg accepted the opportunity, and slaughtered a hundred enemies under the Erdtree's banner. His glorious accolades warranted Erdtree Burial and, upon his death, an exception was made to grant his spiritual return to the Erdtree. Conversely, Engvall refused, choosing to remain in banishment. He instead became a fringefolk hero, and spent his days running a lordless castle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Wings of the Storm did not practice Dragon Communion.
- Banished Knight Engvall likely preceded Godrick the Grafted as the leader of Stormveil Castle. It is also possible that he was the steward of Castle Morne, or somewhere else entirely.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Witch of the Wheel was a practitioner of ancient magic who once dwelled in the Deep Woods beyond the Lands Between. Known for her cunning and deceit, she relied upon guile as both weapon and shield. She was an old companion of the Recluse, sharing in the same arts and knowledge, and in time became the nurse of the Infant summoned by her counterpart. The newborn being devoured without end, and the Witch was tasked with appeasing its insatiable hunger.

During a later clash of armies, the two witches unleashed the Infant as a weapon. The monstrous creature overran the enemy but soon turned upon its summoners. The Recluse failed to offer comfort or embrace to the frightened child, and the Witch of the Wheel was slain in the chaos. Her shadow was shorn away and her essence subsumed, leaving behind a lifeless body.

The Witch of the Wheel was later restored to life at the Roundtable Hold through the power of the Nightlord. In this state, she attacked the Iron Menial and locked him in the crypt, taking his likeness to move freely within the Hold. Her activities drew the suspicion of the Recluse, who eventually detected the Witch’s magic within the Vestige of Night. The Witch's old companion sought her out to atone for her death.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown:
The Witch of the Wheel appears in the Realm of Remembrance at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold during the third chapter of Recluse's Remembrance Quest. She has disguised herself as the Iron Menial, and is polishing a sword at the Sparring Grounds. Attack and slay the puppet, prompting her to mimic the Recluse's appearance.

She appears again after defeating Heolstor the Nightlord. Visit the bed area where the Vestige of Night was in the ashen Roundtable Hold and embrace the crying Infant. Return to the bed area after the ending. The Witch of the Wheel thanks the Recluse for choosing to love their infant Night.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Wears the Recluse's Remembrance Garb
- The Witch of the Wheel's magic binds the Night Aspect.
